crawl-batch.batch-max-concurrency.evidence: Implemented at f7e3b96 (branch claude/m2-batch on main 97c2cee): BatchStartRequest.maxConcurrency, an integer 1..4 ('maxConcurrency must be an integer between 1 and 4'), stored on Task.batch and handed to the orchestrator run as its concurrency cap (min(workerCount, cap); the per-host gate and 250 ms interval stay), reported as the cap in force on GET /v1/batches/:id (Math.min(cap ?? workerCount, workerCount)), on the MCP batch_scrape schema and through the SDK; the hosted MCP normalizer keeps refusing it ('unsupported remote tool option'). Live at e3d935e through the local API on 127.0.0.1:8807, HTTPS_PROXY 127.0.0.1:7890 (egress_proxy and evidence.envProxy on every item): A, https://www.data.gov.uk/search?q=energy pages 1-5 (test set #22) with maxConcurrency 1 completed 5/5 success on http in 11.1 s with maxConcurrency 1 reported; the intervals [createdAt - wallMs, createdAt] never overlap (gaps 0.5, 1.1, 1.0, 1.1 ms), consecutive starts 2,908 / 2,603 / 2,011 / 1,688 ms apart, robots_checked allowed with ruleCount 0 on each. Fixture tests in packages/api/test/batch.test.ts: with perHostConcurrency 2 and workerCount 2 a 4-URL batch reaches 2 requests in flight (proven by arrival, not timing) and the same batch under maxConcurrency 1 never more than 1; a cap of 4 on a 2-worker service reports 2; an interrupted batch resumes under its stored cap. Record: research/parity/m2-batch-live-checks-2026-10-02.md.

crawl-batch.batch-ignore-invalid-urls.evidence: Implemented at f7e3b96: BatchStartRequest.ignoreInvalidURLs; the parser names a refused entry by its index ('urls[1] must be http(s)', 'urls[1] is required') and with the option collects such entries into invalidURLs instead (a non-string entry is still 'urls[i] must be a string', a duplicate still 'urls must be unique', none left is 'urls must contain at least one valid URL'); the engine stores invalidURLs on Task.batch and returns it on the 202 (BatchAccepted) and on GET /v1/batches/:id, requested counting the valid URLs; MCP batch_scrape forwards the caller's urls as sent with the option; the hosted normalizer refuses it. Live at e3d935e: B1, {urls: ['https://example.com', 'not a url', 'ftp://x'], ignoreInvalidURLs: true} answered 202 with invalidURLs ['not a url', 'ftp://x'], completed 1/1 (example.com success on http through the proxy) with the same invalidURLs on the status; B2, the body without the flag, answered 400 'urls[1] must be http(s)' and created no task directory. Tests: contracts api.test.ts, api batch.test.ts, mcp tools.test.ts, sdk client.test.ts. Record: research/parity/m2-batch-live-checks-2026-10-02.md.

crawl-batch.batch-errors.evidence: Implemented at f7e3b96: GET /v1/batches/:id/errors?cursor=&limit= (limit 1..1000, default 1000), SDK getBatchErrors, MCP get_batch_errors (also a read on the hosted host): the batch's failed, blocked, cancelled and budget_exceeded steps across every attempt (no attempt filter, so a resumed batch keeps its earlier failures; the crawl route reads the latest attempt alone), each projected to { id, timestamp, url, status, code, error, httpStatus } with code = failureReason ?? blockReason ?? budgetExceeded ?? status and error = the first warning or '<status>: <code> (HTTP n)' plus the robots.txt rule, and robotsBlocked = the URLs whose result is policy_denied with a robots_disallowed trace event and no robots_overridden event (a governance or SSRF policy_denied stays out); 404 for a crawl id. Live at e3d935e: C, a batch of gov.uk electricity-section-5-energy-trends (#26), bls.gov empsit.t01.htm (#18), httpbin.org/status/404 and httpbin.org/deny listed exactly the two httpbin URLs: /status/404 {failed, http_error, 404, 'failed: http_error (HTTP 404)'} and /deny {failed, policy_denied, null, 'failed: policy_denied — robots.txt rule /deny'} with robotsBlocked ['https://httpbin.org/deny'], whose trace has robots_checked disallowed (ruleCount 1, the file's sha256) and robots_disallowed {pattern '/deny'} and no request; gov.uk was success on http and bls.gov success on browser_local after the http rung's 403 bot_detected_generic (channelsTried ['http', 'browser_local']), both absent from errors. Fixture tests: a batch of item/1, private/item/2 (overridden), private/item/3 and missing/4 lists two errors with robotsBlocked [private/item/3], pages with limit=1, refuses limit=1001, answers 404 for a crawl id; an interrupted and resumed batch keeps its first attempt's refusal. Record: research/parity/m2-batch-live-checks-2026-10-02.md.
